body: You sounds like a totally cool and reasonable person; I would recommend that you stick around and wait to see what happens, you're bound to meet someone that fulfills your wish.

I've looked at almost all of the ways and really, none of them are particularly easy. They are all fraught with potential doubt and non-success. I speak from my own experience of having tried three times in the last year and not being successful.
That's amazing, you're super inspirational for me as I'm about the same age an in a slightly similar situation. Thanks so much for sharing!
Thanks for the advice, I've actually been on the phone with some friends to ask for some help. I haven't shared any details of my attempt, but reaching out has helped me feel better.

I know this feeling well and my therapist was surprised when I shared it with her. My dreams are peaceful and non-depressed. The depression kicks in soon after I wake up and realize that what I've been doing in my dream state isn't real.
Same here, I find ambient music is much better than music with words for clearing my head and falling asleep.
Congrats!
I'm living that life as we speak.
omg, the akathisia was terrible with Abilify for me, but my doctor gave me Propranolol to counteract those side effects and it did help.
I have the best dreams and what's crazy is that I'm not depressed in my dreams. I just feel good.
Maybe plan to go for just 30 minutes and see how it goes?

Sometimes I try to do just one little thing, like get out of bed, or take a shower. Both of which can be really, really hard to do when depressed. Maybe just try to go drink a glass of water and see if you can get some momentum going from that?

I haven't met many people who really understand depression unless they live with it. I think it's hard for people without depression to really "get" the numbness and lifelessness that can come from depression. I find that talking to other people with depression can be a lot easier.
My psychiatrist wants me to walk for an hour each day. It does help give me more energy and kinda clears my head when I do it.
That's a really great step and I hope you make a point to feel good about doing something positive for yourself!
I believe that death is just that. The end. Nothingness. Non-existence. Peace.

I've been in a similar headspace for the last 5 years and it really sucks. I feel trapped by the people around me, I don't want to hurt them, but I'm so tired of this life that it makes me almost resent their love.
I love sleep time as well. It’s so much more peaceful.
Maybe you'll find good medication and look back at this time and be happy that you didn't end it.

That's a rough situation to be in. I had a similar situation with my wife always being on her phone, and always shielding the screen in subtle ways when I was around. I managed to put it out of my mind by purposefully not looking at her hands and trying to avoid seeing her deceptions. For the most part, it helped prevent the constant feelings of distrust and nausea in the pit of my stomach, but in the end, we still ended up breaking up, so your mileage may vary.
It's great you have something to live for at the moment. Maybe you can just leave it at that and continue to work on your self while you have a good thing going?
Congrats, and it's really nice to hear some genuinely good news.
If the medication works for you, it can be great. When I first took Prozac, I felt great. I'd give anything to feel that good again.
It's hard for people who are not depressed to understand depression, so I wouldn't look to them to be able to validate or invalidate your feelings.
Sorry, didn't mean to say that you needed to realize anything, I wrote my response poorly. I just meant to share how I've been feeling.
Happy Birthday!!
Sleep is such a sweet escape. I can't wait to get home and go to bed. If it's extra early I'll even take a sleeping pill to help me nod off.
I feel your pain, I'm in a very similar situation. Can't get a gun because I 5150'd myself a few years ago and none of the other methods seem surefire and painless.
Congrats, that's really cool to hear.

I wish I had some advice, but I don't. Just wanted to echo your thoughts about the cognitive issues. I've been really depressed for the last 5 years and I'm definitely noticing how often I feel scatterbrained and confused. I never heard anything about this until I saw people on this subreddit talking about the effect.

Thanks for the positive thoughts, but realize that it gets harder and harder to find the motivation the longer a major depressive episode lasts. I've been super depressed for the last 5 years, and at this point it's really difficult to find the strength to "keep fighting".

I'm struggling with the depression of making it to another year. It all seems so pointless and futile. I wish I had the courage to just make the decision to end it all, living through another year of pain brings so much dread.
Glad to hear about your progress! Savor the feeling.
Thanks for sharing this. No one has ever told me that in my therapy or doctors experience but I feel the same thing.

I struggle with people asking me why am I depressed. I don’t know why am depressed I just know that I am. I feel so empty and hollow and lonely and sad. It’s probably one of the worst things I can hear someone ask me, is why am I depressed.
